title: PHP startup timezone diagnostics can leave a stale cache pointer
summary: A file-based PHP startup diagnostic can create a timezone cache that is freed before an early request diagnostic uses it. Crafted requests can crash fresh workers; code execution was demonstrated locally with known addresses.

severity.rationale: The flaw requires a non-thread-safe build, suitable startup logging and an early request diagnostic. Worker crashes are demonstrated; remote code execution still has additional unproven address requirements.

exposure: The startup diagnostic must use PHP file-based error_log; the FPM log alone is insufficient. The vulnerable window is before the worker completes its first normal request.

params.instructions: Check PHP date extension version and the documented exposure conditions against the cited advisory.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 or 8.5.13. Until then, correct startup diagnostics or use a logging destination avoiding file timestamps, and restart the master and workers.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed component uses the patched release and test the affected workflow with harmless inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
